solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Good man and yet unprogressive

parts.note: ST, short for saint, is a good man in crossword convention
taken as written
yet in the sense 'nevertheless' means still

explanation.surface: A virtuous fellow who nonetheless refuses to move with the times.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: a thing at a standstill is making no progress.
explanation.definitionFit: A standstill is a halt where nothing advances, a state of making no headway at all.

clue.text: Collector emerges clutching rent

indicators.note: the two clue words hold the letters tightly within them, so the run is inside them

explanation.surface: A rent collector appears, gripping the tenant's payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like a payment owed to the collector, but it is the past tense of rend.
explanation.definitionFit: Rent is the past tense of rend, meaning ripped apart, the same as the past of tear.

clue.text: Minority of lawyers could be 90-year-old — not half

indicators.note: only half the word is kept, the front six of its twelve letters

parts.note: someone in their nineties is a nonagenarian

explanation.surface: A small group of lawyers might be ninety years old, though that is not halfway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minority' looks like a small group of lawyers, but it is the legal term for being under age.
explanation.definitionFit: In legal language nonage is the state of being under age, a person's minority before adulthood.

clue.text: Continually hold us up to the mark

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the short word is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: a mark such as a blot is a stain

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep holding us up to the required standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To the mark' looks like the idiom for meeting a standard; 'to' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain something is to keep it up or support it without a break over time.

clue.text: Rain is unusual in this country

indicators.note: being unusual suggests the letters of the word are in a strange order

explanation.surface: Rainfall is rare in this nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a Middle Eastern nation, and a largely arid one, which suits the surface.

clue.text: Fear of redundancy drove him to breaking point

definitions.text: Fear of redundancy drove him to breaking point

parts.words: Fear of redundancy drove him to breaking point
parts.note: a textile worker afraid of losing his job to machines went about smashing the machinery, so breaking point is literal

explanation.surface: A man driven to his limit by worries about losing his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking point' reads as a mental limit, but these early nineteenth-century English workers literally broke the machines.
explanation.definitionFit: The Luddites were English weavers who wrecked new mechanised looms fearing these would take their jobs.

clue.text: Amazed, and so is the organisation

indicators.note: organisation as the act of arranging tells us to put these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone surprised, and the company is too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organisation' looks like a noun for a company, but it is the act of organising the letters of AND SO IS THE.
explanation.definitionFit: To be astonished is to be greatly surprised, a close synonym of amazed.

clue.text: Choose to pay the bill produced by cricket side

parts.note: to settle up is to pay what is owed
the on side is the leg side of a cricket field

explanation.surface: Deciding to pay what a cricket team has run up.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the off side and the on (leg) side.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle upon something is to decide on it or choose it after consideration.

clue.text: A bit of land is being given to the French

parts.note: taken as written
le is a French word for the

explanation.surface: A patch of territory is being handed over to France.
explanation.definitionFit: An isle is an island, a small piece of land surrounded by water.

clue.text: Where to view great partnership?

parts.note: grand means great or impressive
in cricket a stand is a partnership between two batsmen

explanation.surface: A question about where to watch an excellent pairing at the cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a stand is the runs scored by a pair of batsmen together.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandstand is the main covered seating area for spectators at a sports ground.

clue.text: Soldiers in the trenches did this craft

definitions.text: Soldiers in the trenches did this
definitions.meaning: troops digging trenches excavated the earth
a boat hollowed out of a single tree trunk

explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers dug out their trenches, and a dugout is also a canoe carved from a log.

clue.text: The S African flag

parts.note: flag here is a plant of the iris family, and this one is a flowering plant native to southern Africa, not a national banner

explanation.surface: A description of South Africa's national banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' wants to be a banner; it is the botanical name for an iris-like plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Freesias are fragrant flowering plants of the iris family originating in South Africa.

clue.text: Investments in swings and roundabouts will get equal distribution?

parts.note: swings and roundabouts are rides found at a fair
shares are investments in a company

explanation.surface: Putting money into playground rides will lead to a fair split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swings and roundabouts' looks like the British idiom for gains balancing losses; here it means funfair rides.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair shares means each person gets an equal portion, an even distribution.

clue.text: No problem in Baker Street?

parts.note: Baker Street is where Sherlock Holmes lived, and his supposed catchphrase to Watson called a solved case simple

explanation.surface: A question whether the London street has no difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: Holmes's famous (though never quite written) line is 'Elementary, my dear Watson'.
explanation.definitionFit: Elementary means simple or basic, so something elementary poses no problem.

clue.text: Religious passage a tissue of lies

indicators.note: a tissue is a woven web, so the letters are woven into a new pattern

explanation.surface: A scripture passage that is nothing but falsehood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passage' looks like a text from scripture; it is a walkway in a church. 'Tissue of' makes ISLE from LIES.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a passageway between pews in a church.

clue.text: Fruitless tries converted by the French

indicators.note: converted means changed, so the letters take a new form

parts.note: le is a French word for the

explanation.surface: Rugby tries turned into goals by the French were useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Converted' looks like the rugby term for kicking after a try; it turns TRIES into STERI.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterile means barren, producing no fruit or offspring.

clue.text: Not much seen in street collecting tin

indicators.note: the abbreviation for street gathers the other piece inside it

parts.note: a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Little is seen of street collectors rattling their tins.
explanation.definitionFit: Scant means barely sufficient, very little in amount.

clue.text: Relative's somewhere in S France, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us to go by how the place name is spoken

parts.note: Nice is a city on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: A family member lives somewhere in the south of France, so we are told.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a family relation, the daughter of one's sibling.

clue.text: Piece of news I encountered on return

indicators.note: coming back means the word for met is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: encountered means met

explanation.surface: A bit of gossip someone picked up on the way home.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is a single article or report in a newspaper or broadcast.

clue.text: Betray mum and ring head of police

parts.note: mum means silent, and sh is the call for silence
a ring is shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: head of means the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Turn in your mother and call the chief constable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like a mother; it is the word for keeping quiet. 'Ring' looks like a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: To shop someone is British slang for informing on them to the police.

clue.text: Tree that can reach a great height

definitions.meaning: a broad-leaved tree common in city streets

definitions.text: that can reach a great height

explanation.definitionFit: A plane is a tall broad-leaved tree and also an aeroplane that climbs to high altitudes.

clue.text: Preserve Victoria, say, over embarrassing situation

parts.note: Victoria is a well-known variety of plum
a jam is a tight or awkward spot

explanation.surface: Keep Queen Victoria safe from an awkward predicament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victoria' looks like the queen; it is a British plum variety. 'Over' places PLUM above JAM in a down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A preserve is a fruit spread such as jam, here one made from plums.

clue.text: Girl about to set up exciting material

indicators.note: about means around, so the girl's name goes round the other piece

parts.note: Erica is a girl's name

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the little word is read upward

explanation.surface: A young woman is about to set up something thrilling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' looks like 'on the point of'; 'about' is the container and 'set up' turns TO into OT.
explanation.definitionFit: Erotica is sexually arousing literature or art, material meant to excite.

clue.text: Church eminence

parts.note: eminence can mean a high rank such as a cardinal's title, but here it means something lofty rising from a church building

explanation.walkthrough: 'Eminence' suggests a cardinal; it means a high point.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeple is a tall tower with a spire rising above a church, a lofty projection.

clue.text: Trampled, with or without study

parts.note: the past tense of the verb for walking means trampled on its own, and with a word for a study added it still does

explanation.surface: Walked over whether or not one has done any reading.
explanation.walkthrough: Both TROD and TROD plus DEN (a study) mean trampled, hence 'with or without'.
explanation.definitionFit: Trodden is the past participle of tread, meaning walked on or crushed underfoot.

clue.text: Took steps in time

parts.note: took steps looks like acting promptly, but it means moving the feet to a beat

explanation.walkthrough: 'Took steps in time' reads as acting before it was too late.
explanation.definitionFit: To dance is to move rhythmically in steps, keeping time with music.

clue.text: Music sets worker on edge

indicators.note: on puts the first piece on top of, so before, the second

parts.note: an ant is the classic crossword worker
a hem is the edge of a garment

explanation.surface: A piece of music puts a labourer on edge.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthem is a piece of music, such as a national song or choral work.

clue.text: Give us directions for Customs?

parts.note: taken as written
E and S are the compass directions east and south

explanation.surface: Tell us how to find the customs office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Customs' suggests the border office; it means habits or practices.
explanation.definitionFit: Uses are customary practices, as in 'the uses of polite society'.

clue.text: He's a reformed Wimbledon champion

indicators.note: reformed means made again in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tennis champion who has turned over a new leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reformed' looks like a person mending their ways; it rearranges HES A.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Ashe won the Wimbledon men's singles title in 1975.

clue.text: A man takes action as a precaution

parts.note: Justin is a man's name
a legal action is a court case

explanation.surface: A fellow decides to act to be on the safe side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Action' looks like doing something; it is a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Just in case is an idiom meaning as a safeguard against something that might happen.

clue.text: Money provided by dissolute roué?

indicators.note: dissolute suggests looseness, so the letters come loose and are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the accent

explanation.surface: Is a debauched rake paying with cash?
explanation.definitionFit: The euro is the currency used across much of the European Union.

clue.text: Deceived about employee being badly treated

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word wraps around the second

parts.note: misled means deceived
a hand is a worker or employee

explanation.surface: A worker who was lied to and badly treated.
explanation.definitionFit: Mishandled means dealt with roughly or incompetently, treated badly.
